children: Seagate Technology reported a soaring profit in the fiscal first quarter, as the artificial-intelligence infrastructure buildout continues to drive demand for the company's data-storage components.
The company on Tuesday reported a profit of $1.76 billion, or $7.59 a share, in the quarter ended Oct. 2. That compares with a profit of $549 million, or $2.43 a share, a year earlier.
On an adjusted basis, earnings were $7.68 a share, beating the $7.45 a share expected by analysts polled by FactSet.
Revenue rose to $4.23 billion from $2.63 billion a year prior, ahead of analyst expectations for $4.15 billion.

"Data creation, retention and reuse continue to compound storage demand with long term customer demand visibility reinforcing our view of a multi-year growth phase," Chief Executive Officer Dave Mosley said.
For the current second quarter, the company guided for adjusted earnings between $9.00 and $9.40 a share on revenue between $4.7 billion and $4.9 billion.
Analysts currently expect adjusted earnings of $8.66 a share on $4.55 billion in revenue.
Shares fell 7.9% to $614.79 in after-hours trading on Tuesday. The stock closed up 3.7% at $667.85, and had gained nearly one-and-a-half times its value through the close.
Seagate also said it was lifting its quarterly dividend by 2.7% to 76 cents a share, up from 74 cents.
The new payout, equal to $3.04 a year, represents a 0.5% annual yield based on the company's Tuesday closing price. The dividend is payable on Jan. 7 to shareholders of record as of Dec. 23.
